chief_complaint: constant severe spinning vertigo lasting 3 days post-cold
hpi_details: 42-year-old female presents with acute, constant, severe spinning vertigo accompanied by nausea and vomiting for the past 3 days. It is present even when she is completely still. She recovered from a viral upper respiratory infection 1 week ago. Denies hearing loss, tinnitus, or focal weakness.
ideas: She thinks a balance crystal came loose in her inner ear or that congestion from her recent cold backed up into her head.
concerns: She is worried she might be having a stroke or brain aneurysm because the spinning is so constant and violent.
expectations: She hopes to receive a quick-acting injection or pill to halt the spinning and nausea so she can get back home to care for her family.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Vestibular Neuritis is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes a short corticosteroid (Methylprednisolone) taper, short-term vestibular suppressants, and early vestibular rehabilitation, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: constant severe spinning vertigo lasting 3 days post-cold

Key HPI features: A 42-year-old female presents with acute, constant, severe spinning vertigo accompanied by nausea and vomiting for 3 days after a viral upper respiratory infection, without hearing loss, tinnitus, or focal weakness.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Vestibular Neuritis.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Vestibular Neuritis.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Labyrinthitis (has hearing loss) without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Any neurological deficit — would suggest a central cause instead.
management_principles: Plan for Vestibular Neuritis: Methylprednisolone, vestibular suppressants short-term, rehab
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective:
Chief Complaint: constant severe spinning vertigo lasting 3 days post-cold

42-year-old female presents with acute, constant, severe spinning vertigo accompanied by nausea and vomiting for the past 3 days. It is present even when she is completely still. She recovered from a viral upper respiratory infection 1 week ago. Denies hearing loss, tinnitus, or focal weakness.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals normal. Positive spontaneous horizontal-torsional nystagmus beating away from the affected side. Normal hearing to gross testing. Head Impulse Test is positive (abnormal saccade) on the affected side. No focal neurological deficits.
reference_soap.plan: Prescribe a short course of oral corticosteroids (Methylprednisolone taper). Provide symptomatic vestibular suppressants (Meclizine or Promethazine) strictly for the first 48-72 hours only, then discontinue to allow central vestibular compensation. Encourage early vestibular rehabilitation.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Vestibular Neuritis
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Vestibular Neuritis
Implement evidence-based management plan: Methylprednisolone, vestibular suppressants short-term, rehab

teaching.one_liner: Viral inflammation of the vestibular nerve causing constant, severe vertigo lasting days after a cold, without hearing loss.
red_flags: Any neurological deficit — would suggest a central cause instead

must_ask.say: Is the spinning constant, not triggered by movement?
How many days has this lasted?
Did you have a cold recently?
Any weakness, double vision, or trouble speaking?

history.answer: The room has been spinning violently around me for the past three days, and it just will not stop.
Everything is spinning in circles around me. It feels like a true spinning sensation, not lightheadedness or feeling faint.
It started suddenly three days ago when I woke up in the morning. I have never had an episode like this before in my life.
It has been going on continuously for three full days. The spinning does not stop even for a minute, even when I keep totally still.
Turning my head or rolling in bed makes the dizziness much more intense. However, keeping my head still does not make it go away completely.
I have felt terrible nausea the entire time and threw up three or four times over the past couple of days. I can barely keep any solid food down.
No, my hearing is completely fine in both ears. I haven't noticed any muffled hearing, ear pressure, or ear pain.
No, I haven't heard any ringing, buzzing, or hissing sounds in either of my ears.
No, I have not had any double vision, slurred speech, trouble swallowing, facial drooping, or weakness and numbness in my arms or legs.
I feel very unsteady on my feet and veer to one side when I try to walk. I have to hold onto walls and furniture so I don't fall over.
No, I do not have any headache, and my neck is not stiff or painful at all.
No, my heart isn't racing or fluttering, and I haven't felt any chest pressure, tightness, or shortness of breath.
No, I have remained completely awake and alert the entire time without blacking out or fainting.
Yes, about a week ago I had a bad cold with a runny nose, mild fever, and a sore throat. That had just cleared up right before this spinning began.
No, I haven't had any black stools, bloody vomit, or heavy menstrual bleeding, though I've only managed small sips of water due to nausea.
I don't have diabetes, and I don't take insulin or any blood sugar medications.
No, I have never had migraines, and I don't have any sensitivity to bright lights or loud noises.
No, I don't have high blood pressure, diabetes, high cholesterol, or any heart rhythm issues like atrial fibrillation.
I am not taking any blood pressure pills, water pills, sedatives, or sleeping medications, and I haven't started any new prescriptions.
I had a busy week at work, but I was not feeling panicky, hyperventilating, or unusually anxious before the spinning hit.
I thought maybe one of those inner ear balance crystals came loose, or fluid from that cold I had last week got trapped in my head.
I'm terrified that something burst in my brain or that I'm having a stroke since the room won't stop spinning even when I lie still.
I just want a shot or strong pill to stop this spinning and vomiting right now so I can go home to my kids.
I have generally always been healthy and have no chronic medical conditions.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been hospitalized.
I am not taking any prescription drugs, over-the-counter medicines, or herbal supplements.
I do not have any allergies to medications, foods, or latex.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used any tobacco products.
I only drink a glass of wine socially once or twice a month, and I have not had any alcohol recently.
I work as an office accountant and live with my husband and two teenage children.
There is no family history of ear problems, strokes, or neurological conditions.
My last period was two weeks ago and was normal and regular. There is no chance I am pregnant.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 120/78 mmHg, heart rate 76 beats/min, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, body temperature 36.7°C, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Blood pressure 118/76 mmHg and heart rate 78 beats/min upon standing, showing no significant orthostatic change.
External auditory canals are clear and both tympanic membranes are intact and pearly grey without erythema, effusion, or retraction.
Gross hearing is preserved bilaterally to finger rub and whisper; Weber test is midline and Rinne test is positive bilaterally.
Cranial nerves II through XII are intact with normal pupillary light reflexes, symmetric facial expression, and intact palate elevation.

Spontaneous horizontal-torsional nystagmus beating away from the affected side, positive catch-up saccade on Head Impulse Test toward the affected side, normal test of skew, and no paroxysmal nystagmus on Dix-Hallpike testing.
Finger-to-nose and heel-to-shin testing are normal bilaterally; Romberg test reveals sway toward the affected side, and gait is unsteady without limb ataxia.
Normal S1 and S2 with regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs, rubs, or gallops appreciated.
